projects.name: Contemporary House: Real-Time Architectural Walkthrough
projects.shortDescription: An explorable contemporary home built for the browser in Three.js, with first-person navigation and an extensively optimised 3D environment.

process.text: I developed an interactive architectural walkthrough in Three.js, turning a contemporary house into an environment visitors can explore freely from a first-person perspective.
A major focus was preparing and optimising the environment for real-time use in the browser. I brought triangle counts down from 15M to 3.86M.

First-person movement lets visitors choose their own route and viewpoint, exploring the house as a connected space. The house was modelled, textured, and optimised by me directly from floor plans and elevation maps.
I designed the interiors of the space to match the contemporary exterior.

projects.name: Casa de Minas: Interactive Tour
projects.shortDescription: A complete 3D recreation of Studio MK27’s Casa de Minas, featuring detailed landscaping, architectural renders, and a browser-based panoramic tour with interactive hotspots.

process.text: I recreated the house and its surrounding landscape in Blender, developing the scene from architectural modelling through materials, lighting, and final rendering. The project combines exterior and interior views, elevated orthographic renders, and an interactive panoramic tour that lets visitors explore the spaces directly in their browser.

I created the house, interiors, pool, terraces, and surrounding landscape, bringing the architecture and its setting together in one complete scene. Particular attention went to the relationship between the building’s stacked volumes, open terraces, and densely planted hillside.

I integrated pre-rendered 360° panoramas into a JavaScript web experience using a panorama viewer library. Visitors can look around each viewpoint, move between connected locations, and click information hotspots to learn about features within the scene.

projects.name: 3D Virtual Campus
projects.shortDescription: A browser-based recreation of my undergraduate campus, connecting explorable classrooms and interiors to live online meetings during COVID.

process.text: I recreated my undergraduate campus as an interactive 3D environment where students could explore familiar spaces, enter rooms, and join the online meetings associated with them. Built during COVID, the project connected remote college activities to the physical places where they would normally happen.
The experience was hosted on the college’s official CDN and endorsed by the director.

Built for real-time exploration: Recreating an entire campus required balancing architectural detail with the constraints of browser-based rendering. I baked and optimised assets for real-time use, carrying the environment from its authoring tools into a navigable web experience. Multiple rooms could be entered and explored, making the campus a connected environment with usable interior spaces.
The project brought together environment production, real-time graphics, interaction development, and web deployment in an institutionally supported experience created for the college community.

projects.name: Procedural Building Generator
projects.shortDescription: A building generation system written entirely in C# in Unity, producing varied architectural forms with stepped rooflines, repeated façade details, and connected building volumes.

process.text: I developed a procedural building generator entirely in C# in Unity, exploring how architectural rules can produce varied buildings with a consistent visual style. The generated structures combine volumes of different heights with repeated windows, entrances, and roof details. Variations in the overall form create stepped silhouettes, recessed sections, and courtyard-like spaces.
I wrote the generation logic in C#, translating spatial relationships and architectural repetition into a system that constructs buildings programmatically within Unity.

projects.name: Traffic Simulation
projects.shortDescription: A real-time traffic simulation developed entirely in Unity and C#, with vehicles navigating a connected road network through curves and intersections.

process.text: I built a real-time traffic simulation entirely in Unity and C#, exploring how individual vehicle behaviours combine to produce traffic flow across a connected road network.

I implemented the simulation logic in C#, connecting vehicle movement with the structure of the road network. The project focused on coordinating multiple vehicles within a shared environment and handling their progression through connected road sections.

The road layout provides a compact test environment for observing traffic across straight sections, bends, and junctions. Watching the network as a whole makes it possible to inspect how local vehicle interactions affect the flow of traffic elsewhere in the system.

projects.name: Generative Plant Growth System
projects.shortDescription: Plant growth system with artist controllable parameters to let you draw curves and animate plant growth along them

process.caption: Created by animating a single parameter from 0-1.
Animated curves drawn on a surface.

process.text: I made a procedural plant growth tool in Blender, with artist-controllable stem growth, leaf placement & density, leaf mesh, noise control, and stem & leaf size controls. Lets you draw to spawn vines along curves and use a 0-1 slider to grow them. The leaf size and placement changes as the vine grows.

projects.name: AI Background Removal & Colour Transfer
projects.shortDescription: A Blender add-on combining deep learning and computer vision to automate alpha mask generation, colour matching, and shader node setup.

process.text: The add-on integrates U²-Net, a deep learning model for salient object detection, to generate alpha masks directly within Blender, eliminating the need for external image-editing software. It also implements Reinhard Colour Transfer in LAB colour space using OpenCV, allowing artists to match the colour characteristics of one image to another.

Designed to integrate seamlessly into Blender's existing workflow, the add-on provides custom panels in both the Image Editor and Shader Editor. It automatically generates, positions, and connects the necessary texture, Mix, and Color Ramp nodes, reducing repetitive manual shader setup. The add-on also handles Python dependency installation and model weight downloads, simplifying installation and distribution.

By combining deep learning, computer vision, and Blender's Python API, the tool reduces the time spent on manual masking, colour correction, and material setup, making texture preparation and shader authoring more efficient.

projects.name: Make Space: Blender Python Addon
projects.shortDescription: A workflow tool that makes reorganising complex node graphs faster without manual intervention.

process.text: A workflow tool I built to make reorganising complex node graphs quicker. Ctrl-drag pushes nodes left, right, up, or down, creating room for new nodes without manually selecting and moving sections of the graph.

A scroll-adjustable circle limits the affected area, with every affected node moving equally to preserve spacing. The radius can also be disabled to shift all nodes on one side of the starting point, and the tool remembers that choice between drags.
Written in Python using Blender’s API, with a GPU-drawn radius overlay, support for nodes inside nested frames, and cancellation that restores the original layout.

projects.name: Blender for 2D: Python Addon
projects.shortDescription: A Blender add-on that turns a plane into a render-ready 2D canvas.

process.text: I built B42D to skip the repetitive setup that comes with using Blender for 2D work. Set Up configures a top-down orthographic camera, Eevee, and a transparent render background. Align to Selected centers the camera on the selected plane, fits it in frame, and sets the output resolution.

If the plane has an image texture, B42D uses the image’s pixel dimensions. For a blank plane, it uses the plane’s proportions and sets the shorter side to 1080 pixels. A square becomes 1080 × 1080, and a 2:1 rectangle becomes 2160 × 1080.

projects.name: Origin Setter: Blender Python Addon
projects.shortDescription: A Blender add-on that sets an object’s origin to your Edit Mode selection with one shortcut.

process.text: I built Origin Setter to speed up a small task I kept repeating while modeling. To make a door rotate around its hinge, for example, I can select the vertices along the hinge edge and press Ctrl+W. The origin moves to the selection, the door stays in place, and I can keep editing.

I wrote the add-on in Python using Blender’s bpy API. It uses Blender’s built-in snapping to find the target, briefly switches to Object Mode to set the origin, then restores the 3D cursor and returns to Edit Mode. It supports mesh selections and Bézier, NURBS, and Poly curve points.
Saves you the hassle of select geometry -> shift S -> 3D cursor to geometry -> Tab -> object -> set origin to 3D cursor. You can now select geometry -> Ctrl + W.
